draft.title: Workers' rights
card: Trade unions are groups of workers who join together to win better pay and safer conditions. Together they have more bargaining power than one worker alone.
The Labor Party grew out of the union movement in the 1890s. It aimed to win seats in parliament so that workers' concerns could become laws.
In 1907 Justice H. B. Higgins decided a case about the Sunshine Harvester factory in Victoria. He set a basic wage meant to support a worker, a wife and children in reasonable comfort.
The basic wage was based on the needs of a family, not on what an employer chose to pay. It was set for men, and women were generally paid less.
draft.remember: Unions and the Labor Party pushed for workers' rights, and the Harvester judgment based the basic wage on family needs.

a.q: Why did workers join trade unions in this period?
opts: Together they had more bargaining power than alone
They were required to by the Constitution
They wanted to replace the employers' businesses
They could then avoid paying any tax on wages
a.why: A single worker had little power to bargain, but a group of workers could press for better pay and conditions together. Nothing in the card says unions were required by law or aimed to take over businesses.
a.clue: Think about one worker against an employer, then many workers.

b.q: Jack works in a Melbourne factory in 1908 and has a wife and three children. Which idea behind the Harvester judgment best applies to his wage?
opts: It should meet the needs of a worker's family
It should rise whenever the factory makes a profit
It should match what the employer chooses to pay
It should be the same for men and women
b.why: Justice Higgins set the basic wage to support a worker, a wife and children in reasonable comfort. It was not set by the employer's choice. It was also not the same for women, who were generally paid less.
b.clue: Look at what the basic wage was meant to support.

a.best: Together they had more bargaining power than alone

b.best: It should meet the needs of a worker's family
